title: source-backed OLE2 saves reuse validated sector layout with deterministic append and fallback
decision: retained, implemented in litchi-cfb, litchi-ole-common, litchi-doc and litchi-ppt
code_state: public OLE2 sector-layout policy and source adoption; source-backed DOC and PPT embedded-object save routes use Reuse by default; newly-authored DOC remains from scratch
reason_codes: 0652 decision 10 authorizes the OLE2 side of 0617: reuse the source layout by default, reclaim cheap released space, and append when growth no longer fits; policy B (reuse then append in ascending free-sector order) is selected over compaction policy C

the implementation retains source directory and allocation metadata behind explicit adoption, with typed fallbacks for unsupported geometry, topology, changed nonzero class identifiers, DIFAT and rejected plans
the source-backed DOC route reaches the policy through litchi-ole-common::object::Editor::finish; a changed snapshot now carries the same policy instead of silently re-rendering from scratch
the preservation corpus compares every stream and every reused directory CLSID with the source, exercises both MiniFAT cutoff directions, and checks deterministic output across fresh processes

the measurement shows layout retention and append/reclaim behavior; equal-length common-editor edits now use a validated source-backed overlay, but final output is still materialized and no separable 0617 payload-copy saving is registered

accepted_evidence.corpus: 211 of 211 parsed OLE2 fixtures pass stream-by-stream differential, normalized raw source directory records (all metadata fields including CLSIDs, with only planner-owned allocation fields and v3 reserved high size words normalized), reopen and validation checks; 209 no-op/same-length/length-changing saves reuse and 195 length-changing saves append
accepted_evidence.fallback_sweep: 37 tampered DOC source layouts decline safely and 5 parser-admitted mutations retain all stream bytes
accepted_evidence.cutoff: smoke tests cover 4095-byte MiniFAT to 5000-byte regular and the reverse migration, plus shrink/reclaim and append
accepted_evidence.determinism: same-process repetitions and three child-process layout digests agree
accepted_evidence.ordinary_route: the doc_tracked_revision_editor integration test edits test-data/ole/doc/picture.doc through RevisionEditor::finish and observes the untouched table allocation start sector is retained; embedded-object source-backed finish paths call the common ObjectEditor and litchi-ppt explicitly adopts original bytes
accepted_evidence.timing: 24 release ABBA samples on picture.doc in three windows with paired A/A floors; a separate FloatingPictures.doc before/after opened-DOC check and current Reuse/Rewrite container control are recorded without a DOC latency claim

accepted_costs.metadata_retention: adoption reparses the source and retains bounded layout state including the packed mini-stream image; it does not retain a second full source artifact or regular-stream payload copy
accepted_costs.source_shape: directory creation, deletion, renaming and changed nonzero class identifiers fall back to the existing deterministic rewrite path; explicit zero class identifiers clear the retained field
accepted_costs.timing_floor: reuse p50 was 344796–350291 ns against rewrite 246556–249481 ns, or +41.01%, +39.93% and +39.64% in the three windows; the Reuse A/A floors were 1.74%, 1.80% and 2.64%, so this is an engineering regression signal and is not claimed as a speedup
accepted_costs.doc_route_timing: FloatingPictures.doc opened-DOC commit p50 was 2.4811 ms before 70d7768cc and 2.5383 ms after Reuse (+2.30%, no paired A/A floor); current container-only Reuse was 2.9724 ms versus Rewrite 3.9763 ms, a policy control rather than an end-to-end DOC claim
accepted_costs.sink_work: the source-layout emitter still writes every output sector; same-length common-editor overlays read unchanged spans through a composed view before final Vec materialization, so kept_sectors measures placement retention rather than zero-copy output

known_gaps.copy_through: same-length stream copy-through spans are implemented for the source-backed common editor with ordinary-reader validation before final materialization; length-changing and metadata edits still use the source-layout writer, and 0617's 13–30% estimate is not claimed
known_gaps.new_documents: the public litchi-doc Writer creates a new CFB and has no source layout to adopt
known_gaps.performance_scope: no registered latency, allocation, RSS, cold-cache, physical-I/O, concurrency or cross-platform result
known_gaps.difat: DIFAT source and output layouts intentionally decline until a bounded corpus witness exists

withheld: any cross-platform, cold-cache, physical-device, RSS or concurrency result
